text:
maria: quick thought 1: we keep arguing about "runtime SNR proxy" accuracy. propose a small calibration harness that runs sampled in shadow to map the proxy -> measured CE delta vs an FP16 baseline. want buy-in before i spec it.
sam: sounds useful. how heavy is the "measured CE" compute? that's basically running the same prompt on FP16 right?
maria: yep, gold compute = FP16 forward + full logit export for the sampled request. heavy, so keep sampling tiny (0.1% or lower) and run async in a dedicated calibration job.
ali: we need clear labels: the proxy score vs the gold delta. naming suggestion: proxy_score, gold_delta_ce, gold_delta_logprob.
jordan: also record model config: quant_profile_id, seq_len, kv_cache_hit, and RNG seed so we can reproduce.
maria: agreed. minimal schema: sample_id, proxy_score, gold_delta_ce, quant_profile_id, model_name, prompt_len, kv_hit_bool, timestamp. keep single-line events for storage.
sam: what about variance across temperature / sampling op? if model is non-deterministic gold_delta might be noisy. we should run N repeats for same sample to estimate noise.
maria: good point. harness will re-run the sample N=3 by default and record mean+stdev of gold_delta_ce. we can tune N.
ali: perf ops: schedule calibration compute onto a lower-priority GPU fleet or CPU fallback that can run with less urgency. put job in a "calibration" queue.
jordan: privacy: sampled prompts must obey per-customer opt-out. store only hashed prompt id and encrypted payloads if customer allows. redaction pipeline should run before storing.
maria: yep - default store hashed id + metadata, keep raw payload in encrypted blob store with TTL 30d and strict ACLs.
sam: how do we surface results? a daily calibration table and a small dashboard plotting proxy_score vs gold_delta_ce density and a confusion matrix for thresholds.
ali: thresholds: if proxy_score > T_high => likely degrade, < T_low => safe, middle => uncertain. we should compute ROC/AUC and pick thresholds per-model and per-profile.
jordan: ops can then bake per-profile hysteresis thresholds into routing: example rule: if 3/5 consecutive samples exceed T_high -> route to safer profile.
maria: implementation detail: runtime library exposes evaluate_proxy(context) -> float and emit_sample(request) when header x-calibrate:1 is present. default header off.
sam: can we piggyback on existing shadow-sampling infra? reuse the sampling dispatcher and storage connectors. avoids new plumbing.
ali: yes, reuse. but we need a small adapter to schedule the gold-run on GPU fleet. non-blocking enqueue.
jordan: small UX ask: add a CLI tool calibrate-plot --profile <id> that produces the scatter/ROC and writes CSV for offline analysis.
maria: action items: 1) maria to draft harness spec + schema 2) ali to propose sampling quotas and storage TTLs 3) sam to check scheduler/capacity for calibration job 4) jordan to draft dashboard/CLI UX 5) ops-bot to spin a shadow run tomorrow.
ops-bot: ops: scheduled calibration shadow-run 'cal-harness-001' starting 1787661000, sample rate 0.05% :gear:
maria: thanks all. one more: let's avoid conflating proxy improvement with model updates. record model git sha and weights tag so we can correlate.
sam: oh and record quantization backend (e.g., a100-cuda, triton-fp8-shim) - backend differences will matter.
ali: note for later: consider a small "synthetic corpus" of prompts that exercise edge tokens for deterministic baseline checks. good for nightly sanity.
maria: agree. i'll include synthetic seeds in the spec. will post RFC update in #rfc-quant in the morning. :sparkles:
